newsitem.title: JAPAN: Poll shows drop in Japan government's popularity.
newsitem.headline: Poll shows drop in Japan government's popularity.

text.p: The popularity of Japanese Prime Minister Ryutaro Hashimoto's cabinet dropped last month, with its approval rating slipping nearly five points to 51.8 percent, a poll by a major newspaper showed on Wednesday.
The Yomiuri Shimbun poll of 3,000 people was taken last weekend and compared with a similar poll in mid-December.

"The slip is partly attributable to the government's failure to outline clear-cut fiscal reconstruction measures in the draft budget for fiscal 1997 which is now before the Diet (parliament)," the newspaper said.
It said the prolonged hostage crisis at the Japanese embassy in Lima also contributed to the fall in support.
The proportion of people who said they did not support Hashimoto's cabinet rose 5.2 percentage points to 36 percent, while the level of support fell 4.7 points to 51.8 percent.
The newspaper cited discontent over planned tax rises this year and the failure of the economy to stage a robust recovery.
Hashimoto's conservative Liberal Democratic Party is in a loose alliance with two other parties but the cabinet is made up exclusively of LDP members.
